The central challenge is enabling people to credibly prove the authenticity and first possession of a digital record—such as a donation confirmation or an impact report—amid pervasive skepticism and the ease of generating false claims. The venture plans to target both brands seeking to validate their supply chains and consumers looking for trustworthy ethical goods. Primary scenarios include discovering vetted, ethical suppliers (from large, global operations to local, artisanal producers), verifying material provenance with confidence, and providing transparent proof of sourcing standards to end customers. A planned, specific target user group for initial outreach is procurement teams within consumer goods companies participating in sustainability certification or reporting programs, who need a streamlined way to discover vetted suppliers and provide indisputable proof of their ethical sourcing actions to qualify for certifications or meet regulatory requirements. Furthermore, the venture plans to explore the development of a simple, open-source verification widget that any third-party website could embed. The exploration of this widget would follow a simple, phased plan: starting with a public specification document outlining its proposed functionality and integration method, to gauge third-party interest before any code development. To add a measurable goal for this exploration, the venture plans to aim to secure letters of intent from 3 potential third-party websites to embed the widget upon completion of the specification document. This would allow visitors to independently verify the timestamp and authenticity of a claimed ethical sourcing fingerprint directly from a brand's sustainability page. To demonstrate focus and semantic clarity from the outset, the venture plans to define the initial, machine-readable ledger standard explicitly as supporting Fair Trade certification as a concrete starting point for its registry of ethical sourcing standards.

## Delivery Model
The venture plans a lightweight, privacy-first implementation. It would not store sensitive operational details or the underlying event files. Instead, it would generate compact, anonymized fingerprints of that data for ledger anchoring. The goal is a secure and resource-conscious design that maintains long-term verifiability with minimal infrastructure. The team plans to build a clean public interface and supporting infrastructure to make the verification tools usable by its target audience. To further minimize its operational footprint and enhance decentralization—and in alignment with the phased witness network plan—the venture plans to explore a delivery model where the core fingerprint generation and ledger anchoring logic is packaged as a downloadable, open-source toolkit. This toolkit would allow technically adept users or enterprise partners to run the core verification processes on their own infrastructure, while still interoperating with the public ledger and the venture's primary web interface for discovery and standardized verification.

## Revenue Logic
The venture plans to generate revenue through the sale of a subscription service to brands and suppliers for access to the verification ledger, advanced provenance reporting features, and supply chain management capabilities within the platform. An initial free trial period for the subscription service is proposed to onboard supplier and brand partners, with a concrete, measurable condition such as a 30-day free trial or the first 100 fingerprint generations, whichever comes first. To add rigor to the revenue model validation plan, the venture plans to define a specific, measurable KPI for the free trial conversion rate, such as aiming for a 5% conversion rate from free trial to paid subscription among pilot users. The venture also plans to explore potential optional upgrades for enhanced connectivity or integration services for enterprise procurement or certification programs.

## Distinctiveness
The venture aims to differentiate itself by offering a system that merges immediate, tangible proof with enduring digital verification of ethical sourcing. Its proposed system does not just provide a product; it aims to create a permanent, independently verifiable record that the materials were sourced according to specific ethical standards at a specific time, addressing the credibility problem of sustainability claims. This focus on verifiable provenance from a specific, ethical source is presented as a unique safeguard for both consumer trust and material truth. The venture plans to explore a further point of differentiation: structuring its public ledger not just as a tamper-proof record, but as a machine-readable, open registry of ethical sourcing standards. By planning to initially support a defined standard like Fair Trade, it aims to create a new, concrete layer of semantic clarity and auditability that is missing from current provenance claims.
